answer.text: began to move again, which was read as pressure restoring the membrane's volume
answer.line: Paragraph 3: under helium at about a hundred atmospheres, the animals begin to move again, read as pressure squeezing the membrane back.

steps: Read both parts: what happened (the animals moved again) and how it was read (pressure squeezing the membrane back to its original volume).
Match the choice that has both. Sentence 3 says why it mattered: it "appeared to seal the case."

choices.text: stopped breathing and had to be supported by a ventilator
choices.note: Breathing and ventilators never come up. The change the passage reports is movement coming back.

choices.text: needed a far larger dose of agent for the rest of the experiment
choices.note: Pressure undoing the drug might suggest a bigger dose, but no later dosing is described. The passage reports only that the animals moved again.

choices.text: showed no measurable change of any kind
choices.note: The animals began to move again, a clear change. That change is why the result looked like proof.

choices.text: began to move again, which was read as pressure restoring the membrane's volume
choices.note: Both halves of sentence 4: the animals moved again, read as the membrane squeezed back.

choices.text: lost the response to a surgical stimulus that they had still shown a moment earlier
choices.note: Pressure brought movement back; this choice has a response taken away. The surgical stimulus belongs to the compounds in paragraph 5.

lockIt: When a passage reports an experiment, the answer usually holds both the result and how it was read.
